title: Joint pressure and temperature models rarely reproduced six-month Nino 3.4 cooling imbalance in 1951-2025
abstract: We tested whether a measured pressure variable makes a selected six-month temperature cooling imbalance common in seasonal linear models. We used fixed NOAA CPC Nino 3.4 and standardized Southern Oscillation Index records for 1951-2025. The observed normalized cubic change statistic was -0.5076. A joint model with two months of memory and paired monthly residual draws gave 13 absolute exceedances in 1,999 simulations, for a conditional tail fraction of 0.0070. Its central 95% range was -0.3413 to 0.3353. A matched temperature-only model, a joint Gaussian model and a joint six-month model gave fractions of 0.0080, 0.0035 and 0.0100. Adding pressure reduced one residual memory error but did not make this imbalance common. Model memory errors remain. This extends prior same-source temperature-only checks, not independent confirmation. Fixed fitted parameters, prior statistic selection, source uncertainty and omitted state-dependent noise limit inference. We do not reject all linear explanations or establish a physical cause. Code, source hashes, scalar draws, model summaries, a figure and an internal numerical audit are included. External monthly records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Observed cubic change statistic and central 95% model simulation ranges, with temperature memory diagnostics. The ranges are conditional on fixed fitted models, not confidence limits on the observation.
